brief: RBC (equity research, Ken Herbert) maintains Outperform and a $225 price target on SpaceX (SPCX, $139.11) after Flight 15: Starship's upper stage was caught for the first time from Starbase, while the Super Heavy booster exploded in the Gulf after diverting from a tower catch on a low-fuel reading. RBC calls the booster loss insignificant for sentiment and views the catch as de-risking reusability, which could cut costs across Connectivity and AI; it flags sustained post-2028 launch cadence (3,500-7,800 cumulative launches needed for 50GW of orbital compute) as the key catalyst to watch. Post-midterm elections, RBC expects more political headline risk to SpaceX's >$74B Texas/Arizona data center buildout and to NASA contracts, as Democrats push for more competitive, less Musk-favorable awards; RBC still sees SpaceX as best-positioned in space given its lift capacity, and flags NASA's new $10B CLPS framework, helped by ULA's failed Vulcan launch, as a bookings tailwind. On AI, RBC calls Grok a laggard (intelligence index 38 vs. 60) but views cheap open-source models as a demand accelerant, not a threat, for SpaceX's compute business. The $225 PT rests on a 10x multiple on 2029E EBITDA of $280.2B; upside is $275, downside $100.
